Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: explanatory illustration for a Russian web-browser internals lesson, no text embedded.
Primary request: a precise conceptual visual showing how a serif capital A glyph outline becomes a grayscale antialiased bitmap.
Composition: wide horizontal 3:2 image, three clean equally sized panels in a left-to-right reading order on pure white. Each panel contains exactly the same upright serif capital A at the same size and position. Panel one: an unfilled thin violet outline of the serif A, with a few subtle Bezier control points. Panel two: the identical A outline over a coarse square pixel grid, with solid dark cells inside the strokes and graduated neutral gray cells only along partially covered edges. Preserve the triangular counter as white. Panel three: the same A rendered as a clean dark ink serif glyph, with a small magnified edge inset showing square grayscale edge pixels. Two modest arrows connect the panels.
Style: refined technical textbook illustration, flat orthographic diagram, spacious, restrained palette white #FFFFFF, ink #17151F, violet #7C3AED, pale lavender #F5F1FF, neutral grays. Very clear shape correspondence. No mock browser, no decorative objects, no shadows or glossy 3D. No words, labels, numbers, logos, or watermark; labels will be accessible HTML outside the illustration.
Accuracy constraints: rasterization applies to the same glyph outline; outline and pixel mask are aligned; grayscale is coverage at the boundary rather than random noise; this is a conceptual illustration, not a screenshot or claim about a specific OS renderer.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: explanatory raster illustration for a web graphics lesson, all labels will be HTML outside the image.
Primary request: depict rasterization of one triangle as three sequential orthographic panels on a pure white background, wide 3:2 composition. Panel 1 shows a single flat triangle as an outline with three emphasized vertex dots and a faint square pixel grid. Panel 2 shows exactly the same triangle in exactly the same orientation and size over the same grid: pixels whose centers fall inside are colored pale violet, their center sample points emphasized; boundary pixels remain visibly square, no smooth polygon covering the grid. Panel 3 shows the exact same raster triangle with a clean violet-to-teal color interpolation across the filled square cells, while the pixel grid and stepped edge remain visible. Simple small arrows connect the panels.
Style: precise premium technical textbook diagram, flat 2D, spacious and easily readable. Palette pure white #FFFFFF, dark ink #17151F, violet #7C3AED, pale lavender #F5F1FF, muted teal #14806A. Outline triangle has three straight edges, not a pyramid. All three triangles match geometrically.
Constraints: no text, letters, numbers, equations, logos or watermark. No perspective, no 3D, no decorative GPU chip, no rays, no extraneous objects. The picture explains a simplified single-sample rasterization concept and does not claim a one-to-one general relationship between fragments, shader invocations, and displayed pixels. Keep enough margin around panels, with no huge empty border.
